facts.heading: Anxiety worsened since September
facts.content: Hannah has been anxious all the time, with the situation worsening since September.
facts.evidence: it's got worse since September

facts.heading: Made deputy head at school
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school in September after the previous deputy left.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school

facts.heading: Taught Year 4 for eleven years
facts.content: Hannah has taught Year 4 for eleven years before being promoted to deputy head.
facts.evidence: I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Feels incompetent as deputy head
facts.content: Hannah believes she has no idea what she is doing as deputy head.
facts.evidence: I have no idea what I'm doing

facts.heading: Rehearses staff meeting on Sundays
facts.content: Hannah rehearses Monday's staff meeting in her head mostly on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Imagines staff thinks she is out of depth
facts.content: Hannah imagines staff thinks she is out of her depth and that the job went to a better teacher.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice Year 4 teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: Has not received negative feedback from staff
facts.content: Hannah has received no feedback suggesting she is not capable from her staff or governors.
facts.evidence: No. That's the strange thing. Nobody has.

facts.heading: Rewrote email to governors four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Email was about behaviour policy
facts.content: The email Hannah rewrote was about a change to the school's behaviour policy.
facts.evidence: A change to the behaviour policy.

facts.heading: Afraid Mr Hargreaves thinks she is stupid
facts.content: Hannah is afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think she is stupid.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargreaves has been kind to Hannah
facts.content: Mr Hargreaves has been kind to Hannah and told her in September he was delighted with her.
facts.evidence: He's been nothing but kind. He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feels she is lying to Mr Hargreaves
facts.content: Hannah feels she is lying to Mr Hargreaves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: That makes it worse somehow, because I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Feels like a child wearing mother's coat
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat most days.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was headteacher for twenty years
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years.

facts.heading: Mother retired six years ago
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago

facts.heading: Village named library after mother
facts.content: The village has named a library after Hannah's mother.
facts.evidence: and they've named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother says Hannah worries too much
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hannah does not tell mother about anxiety
facts.content: Hannah does not tell her mother how bad her anxiety is.
facts.evidence: So I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Wakes at 4 AM daily
facts.content: Hannah wakes at four every morning to review her to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning

facts.heading: Wakes since second week of term
facts.content: Hannah has been waking at four since the second week of the current term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.heading: Drinks five to six cups of coffee
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee daily to cope with waking hours.
facts.evidence: Five or six

facts.heading: Feels heart racing and hands shaky
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands during afternoon meetings.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky

facts.heading: Leaves meeting to splash face with water
facts.content: Hannah left a meeting on Thursday to splash her face with water due to anxiety.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water

facts.heading: Feels exhausted from pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels exhausted by the end of every day from pretending to be fine.
facts.evidence: I'm exhausted by the end of every day just from pretending

facts.heading: Partner Ben knows she is struggling
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben knows a bit about her feelings but suggests she should enjoy her job.
facts.evidence: My partner Ben knows a bit. He says I should just enjoy it

facts.heading: Feels guilty and alone when Ben speaks
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and a bit alone when Ben tells her to enjoy her job.
facts.evidence: Guilty, and a bit alone

facts.heading: Partner Ben is an engineer
facts.content: Hannah's partner Ben is an engineer who thinks problems should be fixed.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer, he thinks if something's a problem you fix it

facts.heading: No friends at school anymore
facts.content: Hannah no longer has friends at school to talk to as her line manager.
facts.evidence: Not any more, not really

facts.heading: Misses former lunchtime friends
facts.content: Hannah misses the children she used to eat lunch with in the Year 4 corridor.
facts.evidence: I miss them. I miss my class too

facts.heading: Misses children's first-time experiences
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily moments when children get something for the first time.
facts.evidence: The children, honestly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time

facts.heading: Work now consists of spreadsheets
facts.content: Hannah describes her current work days as consisting only of spreadsheets.
facts.evidence: Now my days are spreadsheets

facts.heading: Accepted promotion to avoid saying no
facts.content: Hannah accepted a promotion because she could not say no to the headteacher.
facts.evidence: I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her

facts.heading: Cried after accepting the promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after going home from accepting the promotion.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried

facts.heading: Tears were about fear of not returning
facts.content: Hannah's tears were caused by fear that she would never get to go back to her old role.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I'd never get to go back

facts.heading: Last relaxed time was summer holidays

facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days

facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday

facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud

facts.evidence: Sending an email once

facts.heading: Feels lighter after stating goals

facts.content: Hannah has not told Ben about the four a.m. incidents.

facts.evidence: I might try this week
